title: docs(runtime): declare that `cluster: false` still registers the authz posture bridge (#12679)
body:
Fixes #12679

Adjudicated **option A** (comment `5439316193`; maintainer batch ruling 「12683 本轮不处理，其他同意」, this card item 5). The posture statement **stays** in `service-cluster` with unconditional registration — no cross-package move. The deliverable is the mandatory declaration at three sites, so the declared-not-equal-actual hazard is pinned in text and in test.

**No behaviour change.** Two comments, one docs paragraph, and a reordered assertion.

## The census first — the card's own confidence gap ①

The card said it had **not** measured how many places assume `cluster: false` means zero plugins, and that "决定了 A 的注释是否够用". Measured on `origin/main` at `96dc446c9`, with positive controls before any zero was read:

- Positive controls: `cluster !== false` matched `runtime.ts:67` and `:78`; `AuthzClusterBridgePlugin` matched 5 files; the plugin id matched 5 files. The corpus is reached.
- **Plugin-count / `kernel.use` call-count assertions in the whole repo: exactly 2**, both in `runtime.test.ts`, both already rewritten by the substrate PR. There is no second or third pin.
- **Code branching on the flag: exactly 1**, `runtime.ts:67`, the correct one.
- **Prose encoding the old meaning: 2**, and both are site 2 in its two homes — the `RuntimeConfig.cluster` docblock and `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` section 8. Both said "skip registration **entirely**", accurate before the substrate landed and not since.
- Seven other `cluster: false` call sites use the flag only to avoid standing up a cluster service; none asserts a count. `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:176` was checked and is **accurate as written** (it names the two skipped plugins rather than claiming zero) — recorded so nobody re-opens it.

**Verdict: the ruling's three declarations reach every site.** Option A was ruled on the argument that the harm is erasable by one readable declaration; that assumption holds — the old meaning lives in prose, in exactly the two places the ruling already named, and nowhere in code.

## The three sites

**1. `packages/runtime/src/runtime.ts` — the registration site.** The comment now states *what* the flag does not mean and *why* the line sits outside the branch, and names the two author-facing copies plus the pin that enforces it, so a refactor that moves the line can see what it breaks. A comment that only said "do not remove" would get removed; this one gives the next reader the reason (`cluster: false` is the loudest case the posture check has, not an exemption from it) and records that relocating the statement to `core` was weighed at #12679 and ruled against, re-opening only if `cluster` becomes a customer-facing public config option.

**2a. `RuntimeConfig.cluster`'s docblock** — author-facing, and shipped into the package's `.d.ts`, so it reaches an integrator in their editor at the moment they write the flag. It now says `false` skips the two *cluster* plugins, names `AuthzClusterBridgePlugin` as the one that survives, why it survives, and that it stays inert on the shipped default.

**2b. `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` section 8** — the same statement for an operator reading the docs site, as a warning callout beside the configuration surface. "skip registration entirely" became "skip that auto-registration".

**3. The pin — and one correction to the card's premise.** The dispatch called `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` a bare count. It is not: `:55` **already** asserted `toEqual(['com.objectstack.service.authz-cluster-bridge'])`. The real defect was **ordering** — the count assertion ran first and aborted the test, so the failure an engineer actually saw when the registration was dropped was `expected 1, received 0`, and the naming assertion never executed. The rewrite makes the **first** failing assertion name the bridge, and carries the contract in its message. The exact-set and count assertions are kept, moved after it. Plugin ids are now named constants, and the sibling default-registration test gets the same identity-before-cardinality ordering.

## Ablation — the pin fails BY NAME

Prediction committed **before** the mutation (`caad4296c`, empty commit) so it could not be edited to match the result. Mutation: delete the unconditional `this.kernel.use(new AuthzClusterBridgePlugin());`.

Mutation proven on disk in **both** directions before anything ran — removed text `0`, injected marker `1`, `hash-object` `eb0a15ff…` against HEAD blob `32fc5d29…`. Restore proven after: byte-identical hash to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean, zero residual markers. `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths seeded from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. No rebuild leg is involved for the mutated module: `runtime.test.ts` imports `./runtime` **relatively**, so it is read from source and no `dist` can stale the result; its own imports were built beforehand (`@objectstack/core` is aliased to source in the package vitest config, `@objectstack/service-cluster` resolves through `exports` to `dist`).

Result: `2 failed | 4 passed`, exactly as predicted, and **both failures name the bridge**:

```
FAIL  cluster:false registers exactly one plugin, the authz posture bridge, and skips the CLUSTER plugins
AssertionError: `cluster: false` must STILL register the authz posture bridge
(com.objectstack.service.authz-cluster-bridge). It is registered unconditionally in Runtime,
outside the `cluster !== false` branch, because a grants cache with no invalidation bus at all
is the loudest case the posture check has (#12679 option A). If you removed that registration,
restore it; the flag skips the CLUSTER plugins only.: expected [] to include
'com.objectstack.service.authz-cluster…'
```

Not one count-mismatch message appears. The sibling test failed the same way, at `toContain(AUTHZ_POSTURE_BRIDGE)` rather than at `3 -> 2`.

## Changeset — argued, not defaulted

**Written**, `@objectstack/runtime: patch`. The counter-argument to `skip-changeset` wins here because the deliverable *is* a statement to readers: the docblock is emitted into the published `.d.ts`, and the docs correction retires a sentence that has been wrong since the substrate landed. A correction whose entire value is telling operators something they currently believe wrongly, shipped with no release note, reaches only readers of the source.

## Verification — union run at `e2abbc548`, the final commit

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` — **197 files, 2890 tests, all pass**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` — exit 0. ⚠️ Stated precisely: this package's `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, verified with `--listFiles` (0 hits for the edited test file), so that green is **NOT MEASURED** with respect to the test edits. Measured separately instead, against the ledger's own program shape: total test-layer errors **217**, exactly the `TEST_DEBT '@objectstack/runtime': 217` entry, and the 3 in the edited file are pre-existing import-level ones this diff does not touch. (This exclusion is the standing ledgered condition of #12511, not a new hole.)
- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — the ratchet's own verdict: `OK — 31 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 214.3s, 1570 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number. surplus: none`. Run on a fully built closure (70/70 turbo build tasks successful), so it is a measurement and not a refusal.
- `pnpm lint` — the **whole** repo, `eslint . --no-inline-config`, exit 0. No narrowing claimed and none needed.
- **30 further gate families**, derived from the real diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` rather than from the dispatch's list, all exit 0: the docs family (`doc-anchors`, `doc-authoring`, `docs-single-h1`, `doc-frontmatter`, `docs-section-name`, `doc-route-spelling`, `role-word`, `docs-redirects`, `docs-audit-scope`, `section-landing-index`), the package family (`cross-package-test-inputs`, `test-source-alias`, `type-source-resolution`, `published-files`, `page-declaration-shape`, `slot-lookup`, `comment-mask-adoption`, `plugin-teardown-shape`, `objectql-double-limit`, `ci-filter-parity`), the test-kind conventions (`engine-double-contract`, `where-matcher`, `query-options-erasure`, `nul-bytes`, `type-check-coverage`) and the changeset family (`empty-changeset`, `changeset-no-major`, `adr-0087-registration`, `changeset-gate-self-tests`, `objectui-changeset`).

Heavy runs went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; every verdict above is read from the gate's own printed line, never from a bare `$?` after a pipe.

## Scope

Option B — moving the statement to `core`/kernel — is **not** touched. It is the recorded fallback if the roadmap makes `cluster` a customer-facing public config option, and that is the maintainer's call, not this PR's.
